name: Hyoscine Butylbromide (Buscopan)
mechanism: Antimuscarinic - reduces GI smooth muscle spasm
contraindications: Paralytic ileus, mechanical obstruction of the GI tract, pyloric stenosis, closed-angle glaucoma, myasthenia gravis, urinary retention where obstruction suspected
interactions: Concomitant antimuscarinic agents increase anticholinergic effects; use caution with other drugs causing urinary retention or tachycardia
monitoring: Monitor abdominal pain patterns, bowel function and for antimuscarinic adverse effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, blurred vision); reassess if symptoms worsen
pregnancy: Use only if essential and after specialist/obstetric advice
sideEffects: Antimuscarinic effects including dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, urinary retention and tachycardia; less central effects due to poor CNS penetration
pharmacokinetics: Quaternary ammonium compound with minimal central nervous system penetration; available oral and parenteral formulations
clinicalPearls: Useful antispasmodic for GI colic and symptomatic relief in palliative care; avoid in patients with suspected mechanical obstruction; monitor for urinary retention
indication: Relief of smooth muscle spasm in GI, biliary and renal colic; symptomatic use in IBS and selected palliative settings
